title: Cypress: running inside the browser, advantages and limits

videos.script: Lesson 8 drove a browser from outside, through a driver. Cypress stands somewhere else. {{inside}} Your test runs inside the browser, in the same window as the shop. A small program sits beside the browser, and every request passes through it. {{queue}} That changes how a test is written. A Cypress command does not run when you call it. It joins a queue, and the queue runs after your function has returned. {{retry}} Each step in the queue is tried again until it passes, or until time runs out. So a list that arrives late is not a problem. {{intercept}} And because Cypress sits in the network path, a test can wait for a request by name, or answer it with data of its own. {{limits}} The same position has a price. One tab. One origin at a time, unless you say otherwise. Fewer browsers to choose from. {{honest}} One more thing, said plainly. Cypress needs a separate download, and the machine behind these lessons could not reach it. So every Cypress file here is shown, and none of them was run. Where a point could be measured without Cypress, it was.
